races.name: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Louis The Fifth
runners_data.comment: A No Nay Never colt bought for 215,000 euros at the breeze-ups and half-brother to a very useful 5-6f performer — Louis The Fifth has the pedigree credentials to make a bold debut showing; dam was a smart juvenile at 8f. Worth taking seriously on breeding alone.

runners_data.name: Sod Hall Lane
runners_data.comment: A Blue Point colt out of a useful 7f dam — Sod Hall Lane makes his debut here and our figures rank him last of five. Unless market support is strong, little to recommend him above better-bred rivals on this occasion.

runners_data.name: By Jove Grace
runners_data.comment: An Inns Of Court filly bought for £70,000 at the breeze-ups — By Jove Grace has an able dam at 6f and makes her first start here. Connections are experienced but she is probably one to monitor rather than back on debut unless the market suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.comment: Closely related to a high-class 6f performer and out of a very useful 5f dam — In The Black is a 320,000gns Havana Grey filly with strong physical appeal and top breeding for a 2yo contest; holds genuine appeal for a first start. The main risk is the unknown of a first racecourse start.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Christmas
runners_data.comment: Experience counts from a debut fifth — Queen Of Christmas came behind a subsequent Group-race candidate at Nottingham and now steps into what looks a gentler opportunity; the stable excels with its youngsters at this venue and she arrives with a debut experience to call on. Should take a clear forward step second time out.

races.name: Bet Smarter With Oddschecker+ EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Enhancing
runners_data.comment: Shaped with encouragement on debut at Newbury — not disgraced over today's distance on good to firm going — and now gets a tongue-tie for the first time to help Enhancing settle. Good connections and scope for improvement suggest a more forward display is on the cards.

runners_data.name: Independent Roze
runners_data.comment: A Bangkok filly out of a useful 5f dam and half-sister to a moderate performer at 6f — Independent Roze is on debut here with modest pedigree angles and our figures rank her last. Hard to be bullish here unless the market provides a positive steer.

runners_data.name: Love Tanya
runners_data.comment: A well-bred Blue Point filly bought for 110,000 euros — Love Tanya is half-sister to a smart stayer and from connections capable of producing a forward debut performance. Worth a look on breeding and connections alone.

runners_data.name: One Shot Kodi
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10 lengths on debut at Redcar, One Shot Kodi needs a major step forward to figure here; our figures rank her fifth of six and the debut run gives little encouragement that she has the class for this level.

runners_data.name: Ruby Moon
runners_data.comment: A No Nay Never filly half-sister to a useful 7f performer — Ruby Moon arrives on debut with a fair family profile but our figures rank her fourth, and the pedigree suggests she faces a stiff ask on debut without a clear market move.

runners_data.name: Silesia
runners_data.comment: Three outings without a win but placed on every start, Silesia is appearing to need the step to 6f to show her best — she found the pace of the front pair too hot last time at Beverley over five furlongs. Acts on good to soft and good, and looks the most solid prospect in this field.

races.name: Download The Oddschecker App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Social Spirit
runners_data.comment: Posted two starts showing progression, including a solid effort at Epsom in a stronger 2yo heat, and the step up to 7f here is an angle that could help Social Spirit — versatile from 5-6f on good to soft and good to firm. Should be competitive, though up against respected debutants.

runners_data.name: Telegraphic
runners_data.comment: A Kameko colt half-brother to a very useful 6f performer out of a moderate dam — Telegraphic makes his debut with an interesting sibling profile and is one to treat with respect; the market will reveal how confident connections are going in.

runners_data.name: The First Drop
runners_data.comment: A Lope Y Fernandez colt out of a moderate dam — The First Drop makes his debut here and connections have shown they can have a juvenile primed first time; one to watch in the market before writing off.

runners_data.name: King Of Persia
runners_data.comment: Unable to land a blow on debut here at Carlisle — beaten six-and-a-half lengths in a maiden — King Of Persia is trained by a top course handler and improvement is expected from that first outing; our figures rank him fifth and he should move forward.

runners_data.name: Mia Fantasia
runners_data.comment: A 40,000 euros Make Believe colt out of a dam who showed fair ability at 8f and half-brother to a useful mare — Mia Fantasia debuts for strong connections who are more than capable of having a juvenile ready first time. Worth watching the market before dismissing.

runners_data.name: Parry Green
runners_data.comment: A Massaat gelding out of a moderate dam, with a half-brother who showed fair form at 7f — Parry Green makes his debut here and our figures rank him last of eleven. Hard to fancy unless betting points the other way.

runners_data.name: Platinum Force
runners_data.comment: A 50,000 euros Blackbeard half-brother to a useful 6f performer — Platinum Force is bred to run well as a juvenile and debuts for connections with a strong record preparing youngsters; deserves plenty of respect on his first outing.

runners_data.name: Ricky Punting
runners_data.comment: Below par at Pontefract last time when held in first-time cheekpieces — finding little and well beaten after being off the pace — Ricky Punting now steps up to 7f, which suits, and tries the gear again. A clear rebound is required; prior form showed enough to suggest improvement is possible.

runners_data.name: Be More Ruthless
runners_data.comment: A Rajasinghe filly out of a smart 5f dam and half-sister to a useful stayer — Be More Ruthless debuts with a handler in good shape but the breeding suggests this is a tough first assignment; our figures rank her ninth of eleven.

runners_data.name: Mrs Mole
runners_data.comment: Shaped with encouragement on her debut fourth at Leicester — not far behind in a 7f maiden — Mrs Mole is effective at 7f on good ground and should go forward from that first start; the form looks solid and improvement is likely as the season develops.

runners_data.name: Wells Fargo Stage
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her debut at Redcar — a major step forward is required — Wells Fargo Stage arrives here with a trainer who has an excellent record at this venue. Our figures rank her tenth, and without market signals it is hard to be optimistic about her prospects.

races.name: Lady Dacre Bell Handicap

runners_data.name: Marry The Night
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Easterby who shows solid form on good ground at this trip, with three placed efforts from five starts at 8f on similar going — tracking Runswick from a handy position is the obvious tactical play and Kirrane's northern course familiarity is a plus.
runners_data.comment: Thriving through the spring with back-to-back wins before a well-beaten turf run at Carlisle last time, Marry The Night's sharper form has clearly come on the AW — first-time cheekpieces the hope of reversing that latest effort here. Effective over 8f on any ground but most comfortable off turf.

runners_data.name: I Can Dance
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in form figures at Haydock on Standard and Heaton Park, but returning from 273 days off is a significant concern, and the unknown fitness level after such a long absence means this three-year-old is a genuine wildcard regardless of ability.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed as a juvenile before a promising third last time — I Can Dance is a well-bred type returning from 273 days off and arrives with upside; effective at 7-8f. The lengthy layoff is the obvious concern going into her first handicap start.

runners_data.name: Pension Pot
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Barron who has been fresh recently (12 days), showed a placed effort on good at 6f suggesting the surface is fine, but a tendency to settle towards the rear means a pace that never truly pressures the leaders will leave this horse short of room to challenge.
runners_data.comment: Third at Chester last time off today's mark, Pension Pot finished with purpose after a sluggish early display and stays a mile on soft, good and the AW; yet to win in her last five starts. Our figures rank her ninth of eleven — needs significant improvement to reach the front end here.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old with a strong record of placing on good ground (four placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs), but often finds herself beaten in similar company and the slow pace scenario suits her tracking style only if she can get close enough to the action early.
runners_data.comment: Unlucky not to finish closer than a length third at Ripon last time — clear improvement on the runs prior — Barley goes in first-time cheekpieces with a top yard in her corner; effective over 8f on soft and good to firm. Yet to win in recent starts but the trajectory is heading upward.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old has a genuine win on good ground at 8f in her recent form, travels prominently, and Joanna Mason's patient northern circuit experience suits — one of the likelier beneficiaries if the race is run at a controlled tempo from the front.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time at a mark just 1lb higher than today's, Harswell Ruby showed she is running to her level and handles today's distance and going. Ranked seventh of eleven here, she is on a competitive mark but needs things to fall her way to take a hand.

runners_data.name: Runswick
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who is the lone pace-setter in this race and should secure an uncontested lead, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a reminder that Dunlop's three-year-old has not won on good-to-firm and has produced most of his placed efforts on soft; the uncontested lead is a tactical asset, but the ground is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Two solid placed finishes since returning, Runswick was denied by the narrowest of margins at Chester last time off a 2lb lower mark — stays a mile and acts on soft and good. Our top-rated horse in the field by a clear margin, the 2lb rise may not be enough to deny him.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Standard for Ian Williams before stepping up in trip, the move to 8f is creditable given a recent 4th at Goodwood, and racing prominently gives this three-year-old a chance to track the pace — the drop to 7f form makes the extra furlong an open question.
runners_data.comment: Good prior form before Goodwood but Aqua Bear failed to see out the trip when well beaten there most recently, and a clear rebound is required; handles 6-7f on a range of surfaces. Ranked eighth here and the first run back is worth treating with some caution.

runners_data.name: Wetsand
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with hold-up tendencies whose recent form string shows no finish better than fifth over this trip on good and standard ground; needs a strong pace to bring hold-up tactics into play, which this race shape is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced and always in arrear in her last several starts — unable to demonstrate any progress on her earlier efforts — Wetsand is effective at 7-8f on a sound surface. The question is whether she can produce what her earlier form hinted at.

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form (9 days) and placed on good ground at 8f, but a genuine hold-up type whose natural style is to come from the back — mapped into midfield on the pace chart because the rear is crowded with similar types, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that this horse will likely find the race run too slowly to deliver a winning late burst.
runners_data.comment: First-time tongue-boot and blinkers and yet to win in her last five starts — Popeye Doyle ran to her level at Wetherby last time over today's trip on a sound surface; capable of a decent effort but inconsistent. Our figures rank her second-bottom here and a bold showing would surprise.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on a horse with two wins and three places from 15 starts on good ground, and genuine hold-up inclination means the field's pace dynamic is working against him — like Popeye Doyle, his true running style sits at the back, and a front-runner-controlled race will test whether Marquand can thread a path through in time.
runners_data.comment: Close second at Carlisle last time off today's mark — moving up through the gears to near-miss form — and a notable jockey engagement adds to the appeal for Geo; acts at 7-8f on a sound surface. Ranked sixth here but the trajectory is clearly improving.

runners_data.name: Pepsea
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning just one day after a previous entry (1-day LR flag warrants scrutiny), with four consecutive fourths on good and soft ground suggesting consistent but non-winning form; Grant Tuer's runner is an unknown quantity on this surface pattern and the unresolved running style makes tactical planning speculative.
runners_data.comment: All four starts showing a pattern of close finishes without quite getting there — Pepsea ran to her level at Carlisle yesterday, just fading in the closing stages of a novice at this track; the yard in good shape and the switch to handicap company on today's going opens another door. Well worth a look on her first start from a handicap mark.

races.paceDynamic: Runswick is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals likely to contest the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this flat Carlisle mile on good-to-firm ground. Marry The Night and Harswell Ruby are the natural prominent racers who will look to track close behind, meaning the first two furlongs should establish a clear pecking order without a scramble for position. The field does hold more hold-up and midfield types than can realistically settle in their preferred spots — Popeye Doyle and Geo are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into the midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded, but their actual running style means they will have ground to make up late. With one uncontested leader setting a fair but not pressured tempo on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Runswick in a handy position, conserve energy in the first half, and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs where Carlisle's flat finish rewards those who have avoided trouble and travelled smoothly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Runswick Leads, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Runswick dictates an uncontested lead and the race is run at a fair but unhurried pace, rewarding those who track in first or second position.
scenarios.body: If Runswick dictates an uncontested lead and the race is run at a fair but unhurried pace, rewarding those who track in first or second position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Runswick goes unchallenged and slows the race to a crawl, gifting a soft lead that allows the front-runner to dictate and sprint clear.
scenarios.body: If Runswick goes unchallenged and slows the race to a crawl, gifting a soft lead that allows the front-runner to dictate and sprint clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get In, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and backmarkers who have settled mid-division get a fast enough surface to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely honest and backmarkers who have settled mid-division get a fast enough surface to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Horses Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine end-to-end gallop develops against expectations and the closers find the ground riding quick enough to produce a late swoop.
scenarios.body: If a genuine end-to-end gallop develops against expectations and the closers find the ground riding quick enough to produce a late swoop.

watchPoints.text: Runswick's ground form is almost entirely on soft/heavy — if the good-to-firm strip rides quicker than expected, watch for signs of Tudhope dropping back through the field rather than holding the lead, which would collapse the dominant scenario.

Geo and Popeye Doyle are both true hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map; if either drifts to the back as is their natural instinct, they will need an unusually strong pace to land a blow and punters should note the STYLE_FIT discount on both.

I Can Dance has been off 273 days — Connor Beasley is an experienced handler of comeback horses on this circuit, but a market move without corresponding trial evidence should be treated with scepticism given the fitness unknown.

Pepsea's 1-day last-run flag is unusual and may indicate a withdrawn entry or administrative entry rather than a genuine recent run — confirm race-day fitness and whether this runner is a reliable participant before any assessment.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for the 3:30 slot — the surface is faster than the declared Good, which marginally favours horses who have previously handled quick ground and may stretch the stamina of any runner whose form is built on softer conditions.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Eternal Stakes (Fillies' Listed)

runners_data.name: Assaranca
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly trained by Hannon whose recent form shows consistency at 7f on good ground; similar going record of 2 wins and 5 places from 13 runs gives confidence, but a true closer needing a strong pace that this race shape is unlikely to supply.
runners_data.comment: Positioned too far off the pace at Epsom last time, Assaranca still shaped with promise in a strong Listed heat, suggesting there is ability to show at this level; effective over 7-8f on any surface. A repeat of her best is needed to figure from stall nine here.

runners_data.name: Classic Cuvee
runners_data.note: Varian-trained hold-up filly with a strong 7f good-ground record (1W 2P from 5 comparable runs) and a Listed-level win on her CV; 32 days off is manageable, but she needs the pace to be genuine to deliver her late effort, which is the key uncertainty here.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers go on for the first time and Classic Cuvee likely found a Listed contest too hot for her last month — comfortably held on form that had previously been better. Effective over 7f on a sound surface, a sharper display is required to land a blow here.

runners_data.name: Confide In Me
runners_data.note: In only two career starts she has won at 7f on standard and placed at 6f on good, showing promise; her natural inclination is to race prominently, but with the front slots already occupied she will be crowded out of that position and asked to do something different — Jack Jones's yard has been quiet (0/13 T14).
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced after just two recent starts, Confide In Me matched her debut form when runner-up at Redcar last time, yet steps into significantly tougher company now. Acts over today's distance and going, but a major leap forward is needed to threaten at this level.

runners_data.name: Ellusive Butterfly
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner at OR 100 and the race's sole confirmed front-runner for Burke; her good-ground record at 7f shows limited wins (0W 0P from 4 sim-going runs) and she drops slightly out of role stepping into a controlling lead role, but no rival will challenge her for the front and she sets the entire pace narrative of this race.
runners_data.comment: Winning form at Listed level in a 7f heat last time out makes Ellusive Butterfly a real contender here — effective on any going and versatile from 7-8f. Now carries a penalty though, which is the one thing rivals will be hoping tells against her.

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained filly with a fine 7f good-ground record (1W 3P from 6 runs) and genuine class in the field; naturally a pace-pressing type who wants to be close to the action, but with Ellusive Butterfly going forward she will find herself further back than ideal — Tom Marquand's quality could compensate if she settles.
runners_data.comment: Albaydaa has two wins in her last five starts and arrived at this level in excellent heart, taking a handicap here last time with a narrow but decisive display showing real tenacity. Effective from 6-7f on a range of surfaces, she tops our figures and has scope for more at this grade.

runners_data.name: Applesandpears
runners_data.note: Two wins at 6-7f on good/standard ground (Bethell yard, Tudhope aboard) and a genuine front-pressing attitude; pushed into a midfield role by the race shape, she will be racing out of her comfort zone and the 25-day turnaround is straightforward, but her best form has come when bowling along up front.
runners_data.comment: Placed here at Carlisle last time, which gives Applesandpears a course angle to cling to, and she handles today's distance and going. Our figures rank her ninth of ten, however, and she needs to find considerably more to threaten the market leaders.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Scott-trained prominent racer who has a 7f good-ground win on her record and finds a natural home tracking Ellusive Butterfly; 18 days since last run is fine and Jason Hart can ensure she sits close to the pace — her finishing effort in scenario A is live and she has the tactical speed this shape rewards.
runners_data.comment: A competitive sort who fits well at 6f on testing ground and has done enough over today's trip to suggest she belongs at this level; Figjam ran down the field over 7f last time, a flat effort, and the return to her best form is required. The ability is there — consistency is the question.

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: Fahey's runner has been consistent at 6-7f on good ground (2W 3P from 7 sim-going runs) and Barry McHugh rides; her recent form figures of 3-7-3 show she frequently finishes mid-pack, and she needs everything to fall right from a prominent position to challenge the principals.
runners_data.comment: Close-up third at Musselburgh last time — just two lengths behind the principals — Golden Palace has the class and stamina for today's trip and goes well on a sound surface. Yet to get her head in front in recent starts, but capable of a sharp effort at this grade.

runners_data.name: Just A Girl
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up filly is consistent at 7f on good ground (1W 4P from 9 runs) and Connor Beasley knows her well; her form figures of 2-2-4-3-7 show a horse who regularly finds the principals too good late, and a measured pace will not create the gaps she needs to make her run count.
runners_data.comment: Proximity at Carlisle last time — a close second in a 7f handicap here — gives Just A Girl a strong course-and-distance angle, and she handles today's ground. Our figures rank her eighth in this ten-runner field, however, and she requires considerably more to reach the front end.

runners_data.name: Stimulative Trip
runners_data.note: Menuisier's filly has a 7f good-ground win to her name and good raw form, but 51 days off is the longest absence in the field and her last two runs (9th, 6th) are a concern; a prominent-style runner by nature who arrives fresh, making her pace intentions on returning from a break somewhat uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Placed on the clock at Chantilly on her last start, running to level beaten a little over three lengths, Stimulative Trip handles today's distance and going and arrives here with a jockey who knows this course well retained. Two disappointing finishes before that win are the main concern.

races.paceDynamic: Ellusive Butterfly is the one confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine rival prepared to press her hard from the gates, she is set to control a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground over Carlisle's flat 7f. Figjam and Golden Palace will attempt to track close up in her slipstream, creating a compact, organised pace dynamic rather than an aggressive burn — the tempo should be honest but far from frenetic, which limits the advantage for the pure hold-up brigade. This field carries more genuinely prominent-natured horses than the race shape can accommodate: Albaydaa, Applesandpears and Confide In Me are all natural pace-pressing types redistributed to a midfield mapping because Ellusive Butterfly and the front few leave no room, meaning those three will be forced into roles that don't suit them naturally. The resulting shape — a controlled solo lead, a tightly-grouped chasing pack, and true hold-up horses unable to generate a strong enough closing move on a flat track — emphatically favours horses that can travel prominently just off the pace and deliver their effort without needing a strong gallop to be set up for them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ellusive Butterfly Controls, Prominent Track
scenarios.trigger: If Ellusive Butterfly dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the race resolves as a tactical exercise run from the front.
scenarios.body: If Ellusive Butterfly dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the race resolves as a tactical exercise run from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the honest-but-uncontested pace produces a breakaway scenario and Ellusive Butterfly quickens clear before the field can respond.
scenarios.body: If the honest-but-uncontested pace produces a breakaway scenario and Ellusive Butterfly quickens clear before the field can respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely stronger than anticipated and the leaders empty, allowing a sustained late run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely stronger than anticipated and the leaders empty, allowing a sustained late run from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Disrupted Race Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple would-be prominent runners jostle for early position, creating an uncharacteristically hot pace that blows the race wide open.
scenarios.body: If multiple would-be prominent runners jostle for early position, creating an uncharacteristically hot pace that blows the race wide open.

watchPoints.text: Ellusive Butterfly's unchallenged control of the pace is the single biggest tactical factor — if she gets away cleanly and no rival forces her hand, the entire race shape forms around her and hold-up runners are effectively racing for minor honours.

Albaydaa, Applesandpears and Confide In Me are all genuine front-pressing types who want the same real estate near the pace; watch the opening furlong for jostling that could disrupt the expected orderly race shape and spike the tempo unexpectedly.

Classic Cuvee's hold-up profile is reliant on a truly run race — if the pace is as controlled as expected, Ray Dawson will need to be creative tactically to manufacture enough momentum for her to reel in the leaders from the back.

Stimulative Trip returns from 51 days off and Menuisier's string has had only 2 winners from 22 runners in the past 14 days — fitness and freshness on the first run back should be monitored against her early pace intentions.

The Good to Firm ground (confirmed across all races at Carlisle today) is the fastest surface in the field's recent experience for several runners — check for any that have visibly underperformed or shown going concerns when conditions have been this sharp.

races.name: Stablemate By AGMA Carlisle Bell Handicap

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a recent win at 8f on Good and solid sim-going record of 3 wins in 10; Christian Howarth is a 5lb claimer adding value here, but 39 days off and a big field makes getting a clear run on the outside a concern.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newmarket last time off a mark just 1lb lower than today's, Canvas ran to her level on a sound surface over 8f and is capable of a decent effort here. Our figures place her fifteenth of seventeen, however, and she needs considerably more to reach the frame in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good just 11 days ago for Mark Dods whose yard is firing (3 from 27), but a genuine hold-up horse naturally suited to racing from the rear — this huge field means he is unlikely to get the true rearward position he needs; sim-going rate of 10 from 15 is respectable.
runners_data.comment: Carrying a hood for the first time and having been keen and unable to see out the trip last time at the same mark as today, Glenfinnan needs a cleaner race here; still weighted competitively on earlier form and handles soft and good to firm. A big unknown with the new headgear.

runners_data.name: Vixey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 210 days off for Stuart West whose yard is 0 from 2 recently — the long absence is the key concern, but she has strong form at this trip on Good ground and the tactical position suits her style perfectly if fit enough.
runners_data.comment: Away 210 days — a lengthy absence — and having been far too keen in the early stages last time, Vixey faces a stiff task on her return. Acts over 7f on a sound surface and not soft; our figures rank her last of seventeen and a bounce-back from that effort is essential.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with a Good to Firm win at 8f, though his last five runs all came on Soft or Heavy ground; the shift to faster conditions today is worth monitoring, but he holds his position naturally and could be involved from the front without fighting for space.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces and a solid third last time over today's distance and going — Naples is effective from a mile to 10f on heavy and good. Not without a shout in a wide-open field, though our figures have her ranked fifth overall.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Tom Barron horse 8 days since his last run — drops into midfield on the map but his natural inclination is to race from well off the pace, a style that is unlikely to be served by what looks like a controlled tempo; his 3rd at 8f on Good is the best going evidence he offers.
runners_data.comment: Keen and unable to see out the mile at Thirsk eight days ago, Degale has a patchy recent record and is yet to win in her last five starts; acts at 8f on a sound surface. Our figures rank her sixteenth here and a run close to her very best is needed just to figure.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: 117 days off the track is the dominant concern for Joanna Mason's mount; she is a genuine hold-up type forced mid-pack in this shape, and her sim-going score of just 3 from 15 on similar ground adds further doubt — form tailed off badly in recent starts too.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for 117 days, Enola Grey returns from a break with the bulk of her better form coming on the AW; she handles today's distance and going but this is turf after a long absence. A return to form is entirely possible with fitness on her side.

runners_data.name: Persuasion
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse with a 7f win on Good to Firm just 11 days ago; he has strong trainer form from Tim Barron's yard but is mapping into a midfield berth rather than his ideal position and his six most recent efforts all came over 7f, making the step to a mile a live query.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time off 86 — 1lb higher than today — Persuasion ran to her level and the switch back to a mile is a genuine positive given her 7f profile; acts on any ground. The main risk is that she has been below her best in recent starts and needs to recapture earlier form.

runners_data.name: Lexington Jet
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with blinkers registered, trained by Donal Loughnane whose yard is hitting form (4 from 23 in 14 days); won at 8f on STA and 7f on Good, and the drop back to a mile after a 10f run last time is intriguing — but his GOO sim-going record of just 2 from 15 is thin.
runners_data.comment: Found wanting over 10f last time when sixth at the top of the weights, Lexington Jet drops to a more suitable trip here and clearly enjoys getting out in front; three wins in his last six on good and AW. Our figures rank him fourteenth, though, and the drop back to preferred conditions is the main selling point.

runners_data.name: Billyb
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer carrying a big weight (141lbs) for Craig Lidster's stable, last ran 11 days ago finishing unplaced; his Good going record is poor (sim-going 11 from 15 off the frame), and at his age with this weight he needs things to go very right.
runners_data.comment: Keen and raced off the pace last time at York where she ran down the field, Billyb is usually held up and needs things to unfold more favourably here; effective from 7-10f, acts on a range of surfaces. A clear rebound from that effort is required and she gets first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Jim Goldie's yard (8 from 47 in 14 days) but carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he may not fully commit to the lead; all five recent runs came at 8-10f on Good or Soft and he hit the frame five times at this trip, making him a genuine player if he does dominate from the front.
runners_data.comment: Previously in fine shape with three placings from four starts, Altareq was well below par when well beaten at York most recently — unable to get into the race from off the pace. A top jockey and prior form over a mile on a sound surface give him strong credentials if that run is discounted.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Good and again at 8f on STA, with two wins from nine Good-ground starts — a reliable hold-up horse for Phillip Makin who has placed him well; equipped with a p-marker (hood/visor previously), 25 days off, and a clean record at this distance, he is one of the more credible closers if the pace does bite.
runners_data.comment: Landed a 7-8f handicap at Carlisle last time with authority off a 3lb lower mark, finishing well under pressure — Priapos has two wins in his last five starts and handles any ground. The yard is in good heart and first-time cheekpieces add interest; stepping up 3lb is the only reservation.

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: Tim Barron's prominent racer has been a serial runner-up — five seconds at 8f in his last five, including two on Good ground; 13 days since his last run, no concerning headgear, and he fits the pace shape perfectly as a horse who can track early and sustain a challenge.
runners_data.comment: A pattern of consistent placings in recent outings — placed five times in five starts without adding to her tally — Swift Salian held her level at Nottingham last time off the same mark as today; effective from 8-9f on any surface. A reliable yardstick who needs a slice of luck to get her head in front.

runners_data.name: Leadenhall
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won twice at 8f on Good and runs just four days after his last race, suggesting Easterby is happy and the horse is thriving; his T14 record of 8 from 104 is high volume but low strike rate — however, positional style and course form are strong assets here.
runners_data.comment: Leadenhall took two wins from his last five starts, landing a tight finish at Nottingham just four days ago off the same mark here — running keenly but finishing well under a positive ride. A top trainer here at Carlisle, no penalty to carry, and a claiming jockey: the one to beat at the weights.

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in his natural element at 8f on Good, with five consecutive top-six finishes at that distance on similar ground — tp (tongue-tie/cheekpieces) adds consistency; squeezed into midfield on the map rather than his true rearward berth, so rely on his place record rather than a win conversion.
runners_data.comment: Held up and needing pace to target, Rajapour wore too much ground off at Wetherby last time in first-time combined headgear; effective around 8-9f on any going. Our figures rank her thirteenth, and she needs a strong gallop and the gear to spark the improvement required.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer whose last five runs were all at distances between 9 and 17 furlongs; dropping sharply back to a mile for Ian Jardine and Adam Mullen, having raced just five days ago — the trip contraction and map displacement both work against him finding his best form here.
runners_data.comment: Second at Ayr five days ago off the same mark, Mr Lincoln ran solidly but appeared to find the flat mile insufficient on stamina grounds. Acts on soft and good from up to 13f; yet to win in recent starts but placed form is consistent and he will not be far away.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tom Easterby's hold-up horse wears blinkers and has run at 9-10f in all recent starts; the step down to a mile on quicker ground than he typically encounters (sim-going 12 from 15) represents a significant question mark, and his out-of-role position in midfield rather than the rear adds further doubt.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers on for the first time and a trainer in good form — Financer is a generally consistent type who ran to her level at York last time off a 2lb higher mark than today's; suits 9-10f on any ground. Yet to win in recent starts but rated our second-best horse in the race.

runners_data.name: Be Frank
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' hold-up horse has finished in the top half just once in his last five starts, all at 7-8f on Soft or Good; 12 days since his last run, his Good-ground form is modest and his natural hold-up style is compromised by this race shape — wins in this type of race have been absent for some time.
runners_data.comment: Trainer out of form at 4% strike rate over the last fortnight, and Be Frank has produced five consecutive well-beaten efforts — prominent at Chester last time but never landing a blow, beaten five-and-a-half lengths. Acts over 7f to a mile on a sound surface and has a workable mark if returning to something like her better level.

races.paceDynamic: Altareq is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, critically, carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he may not fully commit to the lead role — nonetheless he is the most likely horse to set the early tempo on Good to Firm ground over this flat Carlisle mile. With no genuine challenger pressing him hard from the front, he should control a sustainable, even gallop that neither burns off the field nor creates a truly strong pace scenario. The large field is heavily dominated by hold-up and midfield types, many of whom are redistributed from their natural rear positions — Glenfinnan, Degale, Enola Grey, Rajapour, Mr Lincoln, Financer and Be Frank are all genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield on the map because the field simply cannot accommodate them all at the back. With so many horses unable to secure their preferred position, those who can race prominently without fighting for space — Vixey, Naples, Swift Salian and Leadenhall — will enjoy a significant positional advantage and are best placed to exploit the controlled tempo. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can slot in early behind Altareq and hit the rising final furlong full of running, rather than true closers who will find the pace insufficient to set up a late sweep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Altareq controls a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent trio of Vixey, Swift Salian and Leadenhall slot in close behind, dictating from the front two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Altareq controls a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent trio of Vixey, Swift Salian and Leadenhall slot in close behind, dictating from the front two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Runs Free
scenarios.trigger: If Altareq overcomes his STYLE_FIT concerns and dictates from the front at a truly uncontested, comfortable clip, relaxing through the race and kicking clear at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If Altareq overcomes his STYLE_FIT concerns and dictates from the front at a truly uncontested, comfortable clip, relaxing through the race and kicking clear at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sharp Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses burn each other off in a scramble for position and the pace accelerates enough in the middle mile to open the race up for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If the prominent horses burn each other off in a scramble for position and the pace accelerates enough in the middle mile to open the race up for hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Big Field Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early interference, position shuffling and a compressed finish where horses racing wide or mid-group are disadvantaged by course geography.
scenarios.body: If the large field causes early interference, position shuffling and a compressed finish where horses racing wide or mid-group are disadvantaged by course geography.

watchPoints.text: Altareq's willingness to lead cleanly must be watched at the start — if he misses the break or refuses to stride on, the race loses its only confirmed pace-setter and the shape collapses into a bunch finish that the prominent horses can no longer exploit.

Swift Salian's record of five consecutive seconds suggests a horse who gets himself into position but cannot quite assert — watch whether William Pyle sends him up to challenge early or allows the habit of settling for second to repeat itself in a big field.

Vixey's 210-day absence makes her fitness a live concern; if she shows any sign of blowing early in the parade ring or races free under Aiden Brookes after such a long break, discount her chance significantly despite the appealing positional profile.

With seven redistributed hold-up horses compressed into midfield, the race could become severely congested on the turn into the straight — watch how much room Priapos and Canvas get at the critical two-furlong point, as a single check could end their each-way chances instantly.

Tim Barron saddles three runners (Degale, Persuasion, Swift Salian) — stable tactics could see Swift Salian used as a positional stalking horse to set things up, so monitor which of the three receives the strongest market support in the final minutes before the off.

races.name: Stablemate By AGMA Cumberland Plate Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Unresolved running style (U) is a concern for race-reading purposes; T D Jardine runner with Tom Marquand up, most recent form shows finishes of 4-4 over 10f on good ground and a third over 12f on heavy, suggesting stamina is present but winning form is elusive; 23 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newbury last time at what looks about British level suggests Wanderlust needs more to compete here, and she is already ranked sixth on our figures. A trainer in good form and proven stamina from 10-12f on soft and good are genuine points in her favour.

runners_data.name: Wine Dark Sea
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's 4yo has won twice over 12f including on good and standard going, and carries the STYLE_FIT flag as it is racing here as front-runner rather than in a more prominent tracking role — the uncontested lead is its chief asset today, and Lewis Edmunds should capitalise on the lack of pace pressure; 46 days off, watch for fitness.
runners_data.comment: Sharp form at Ascot last time when landing a handicap with something to spare off a lower mark makes Wine Dark Sea among the stronger claims in this field; effective over 12f on good ground and the AW. The step up to a competitive Class 4 off a higher mark is the one caveat.

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: Dual winner over 12f on good ground for David McCain, making this trip (1m3f) a sensible step; wears a hood (hg:t) and arrives 47 days fresh, but has decent recent Goodish-ground form and shapes as one of the main threats from a prominent position to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Held to her level at Chester last time — fifth over 12f on a sound surface — Secret Beach arrives here in first-time headgear and handles today's trip. Our ratings place her tenth of twelve, however, and she needs to step up markedly to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo hold-up type has been running over 10f, which is a shade shorter than this 1m3f test; form figures of 4878 are unimpressive, and similar-going record (3/8, 1W1P) is modest — arrives just 11 days after last run which is a positive freshness indicator for this yard.
runners_data.comment: Came home well from off the pace at Chester most recently, finishing not far behind the principals, though without a win in her last five starts Golden West has questions to answer. A top trainer provides a yard angle here at Carlisle and she stays 8-10f.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston 6yo wearing a hood (hg:b), winner over 12f on standard going and placed over 13f on good — this trip is squarely in range; 28 days since last run, and a late-running profile that needs the pace to be honest to get involved; one of the more credible hold-up threats.
runners_data.comment: Third at Hamilton last time off a mark just a pound higher than today's, Ludo's Landing goes in first-time blinkers and acts over today's trip and going; a trip range of 10-13f makes today's stamina test manageable. The new headgear means there is an unknown element.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Goldie's 6yo has won over 14f on good ground and been placed over 16f, so the 1m3f trip here is at the shorter end of his best; wears a hood (hg:p), prominent runner who will press early; recent win 9 days ago is a strong fitness flag and Mulrennan is an aggressive front-of-the-field operator.
runners_data.comment: Winning at Carlisle last time with a willing display off a 5lb lower mark — and with a jockey who has an excellent record at this track back aboard — gives Trojan Sun obvious claims despite a penalty. Acts on any turf ground over a mile and beyond; first-time cheekpieces the variable, and the higher weight is the concern.

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: Lengthy absence of 120 days (jockey 40 days) is the dominant flag here — wears a hood (hg:tp) and has form over 17f on good ground suggesting stamina, but a hold-up profile at a distance shorter than its form peaks and a trainer (Whillans) with a modest 14-day strike rate; treat with caution on return.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces appear for the first time and Inappropriate steps back onto the flat after a handicap hurdle run where she was comfortably held — unable to extend what had been a brief revival. Suits 10f on any ground, but the inconsistency remains the central issue here.

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: Easterby's 7yo is a natural hold-up horse whose best form is over 10f — a genuine closer shown in midfield on this map because the field's concentration of hold-up types means it cannot access its preferred rear position; recent good-ground form shows five runs without a win, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: The trainer has a solid record in this race and Austrian Theory tries cheekpieces after a six-length defeat at York last time where she finished strongest in the final furlong; effective over 8-10f on any ground. Yet to win in recent starts, and a significant rebound from that York effort is needed.

runners_data.name: Eroico
runners_data.note: Todhunter's 4yo is a true hold-up type by profile, placed in midfield on this map due to the surplus of closers in the field rather than by natural inclination — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) signals a meaningful discount to its chance in a shape that doesn't deliver the rear-running position it needs; similar-going record (5/7, no wins) underlines the ask.
runners_data.comment: A long way back at Thirsk last time when tried in a hood and found wanting over the trip — Eroico is our bottom-rated runner here and yet to win in her last five starts. Stays around a mile to 12f and acts on soft and good, but needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's 3yo is in career-best form, winning over 12f on good ground most recently (11 days ago), and has four wins from nine runs — the prominent profile suits this race shape ideally and the 3yo allowance at this stage of the season could be significant; C Lee takes the ride for a yard firing with 7/46 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Finishing strongly at York last time, Dunkeld Dreamer took a tight affair off a 2lb lower mark and has won two of his last six — acts on any going from 7-10f. A live chance off only a modest rise, the main risk being whether recent form is strong enough to hold up at this level.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Goldie's 8yo is flying, having won three of its last six including back-to-back over 11-12f on good ground — a prominent, front-tracking profile that suits this race shape directly; Lauren Young claims, which offsets the weight advantage, but the form line is outstanding and the good-to-firm surface is exactly what this horse wants.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last six — including a comfortable Carlisle success last time off a lower mark — give Alpine Sierra an eye-catching profile, and she is effective from 7-12f on soft, good and the AW. Our figures rank her well down the field, suggesting she faces a stiff task at the weights.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Approach
runners_data.note: Johnston 3yo with a strong recent profile — two wins over 12-14f on good ground and placed in all five career runs — 3yo allowance adds appeal; a hold-up type who has been effective off a strong pace over longer trips, and the 18-day turnaround is workable; one of the most consistent horses in the race.
runners_data.comment: Consistent record of two wins in his last five starts, a sound third last time off the same mark as today, and proven over today's distance and going — Gaelic Approach goes in from the foot of the weights and a drop in trip should suit. Our top-rated horse here by some margin.

races.paceDynamic: Wine Dark Sea is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure horse to challenge for the lead, is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m3f trip on good-to-firm ground at Carlisle. Secret Beach and Trojan Sun will press prominently behind, while Dunkeld Dreamer and Alpine Sierra add to a competitive prominent group that will keep the pace honest without necessarily accelerating it into a test of stamina. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Austrian Theory and Eroico are genuine closers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield positions given the clustering, meaning their ability to produce late runs from their preferred spots may be compromised. This shape — a measured pace from a single leader with a compact prominent group — strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile, rewarding tactical efficiency over raw closing speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Wine Dark Sea sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent group travels smoothly, allowing one to pounce inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Wine Dark Sea sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent group travels smoothly, allowing one to pounce inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Wine Dark Sea's uncontested lead allows it to conserve enough energy to deny the prominent chasers, effectively winning on the bridle.
scenarios.body: If Wine Dark Sea's uncontested lead allows it to conserve enough energy to deny the prominent chasers, effectively winning on the bridle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfielders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop collapses in the final three furlongs and horses dropped in behind midfield are able to produce a sustained run through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: If the gallop collapses in the final three furlongs and horses dropped in behind midfield are able to produce a sustained run through beaten rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Blows Up, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If early fractions are faster than expected — triggered by Secret Beach or Trojan Sun pushing Wine Dark Sea — causing the front-runners to fade and leaving late movers with a proper target.
scenarios.body: If early fractions are faster than expected — triggered by Secret Beach or Trojan Sun pushing Wine Dark Sea — causing the front-runners to fade and leaving late movers with a proper target.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra has won three of its last six on good/good-to-firm ground over 11-12f and races in a prominent style perfectly suited to this shape — a serious player if the pace is controlled and it travels smoothly.

Dunkeld Dreamer arrives 11 days after a 12f win on good ground for Karl Burke, a yard with a 7/46 14-day strike rate — the combination of form, fitness and a race shape that suits a prominent racer makes this a key danger.

Wine Dark Sea carries the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) as it races here in a front-running role — if it struggles to dominate or is taken on earlier than expected by Secret Beach or Trojan Sun, its chance could unravel quickly despite the apparent tactical advantage.

Austrian Theory and Eroico are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to field crowding — if either is unable to access a clear run from its unnatural position in the final two furlongs, their chance of producing a meaningful late effort is significantly reduced.

Inappropriate's 120-day absence (jockey off 40 days) alongside the trainer's weak 14-day figures (0/5) makes it a significant fitness risk despite the stamina profile — monitor in the market and paddock for any sign it is short of work.

races.name: Racing Staff Week Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Rogue Attraction
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up filly whose last win came over six furlongs on Good ground; the step up to seven is interesting but her 236-day absence is a significant flag and she will need the pace to be genuinely strong to land a blow from off the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Away 236 days and in need of a significant return to form having been well beaten in a Listed event last time on unsuitable ground — Rogue Attraction is effective at 6f and gets first-time cheekpieces. Ranked fifth of six, there is ability here but everything needs to click.

runners_data.name: Shushu
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will have the luxury of setting her own fractions unchallenged; two runs over soft seven furlongs have produced a win and a second, and the switch to Good to Firm is her main uncertainty, though her OR drop to 79 keeps her competitive.
runners_data.comment: Getting off the mark at Yarmouth last time in a clear-cut manner — taking a step forward and showing the right attitude — Shushu now tries handicap company for the first time on today's going; effective at 7f on soft and good to soft. Strong handler and further improvement from this mark looks achievable.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Carries top weight of 142lbs and has been absent 138 days; her last two runs came on Standard artificial ground at seven-to-eight furlongs and her record on similar going (2W4P from 15) is solid, but the layoff and big weight ask significant questions from a hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Prior form before that nightmare outing at Newcastle is genuinely decent — Mostar Dreams has won and shown ability at her best across a wide trip range including today's going. Returning from a break and needing to settle after pulling hard last time; if she does, she could be a real danger.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Recent handicap winner at a mile on Good ground with strong Tudhope booking and an active O'Meara yard (7/51 in 14 days); her true inclination is to race from behind, and while the map places her in midfield, in practice she is unlikely to be closer to the pace than that — a factor that tempers her prospects in a steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: Taking to a new headgear combination at Ripon last time, Donna Nook took a tight handicap in a driving finish off a 3lb lower mark — effective from 8-10f on a sound surface. Now 3lb higher but showed enough to suggest she has the class to meet that rise.

runners_data.name: Nanoscience
runners_data.note: McDonald-ridden prominent racer with two recent wins at seven furlongs on Good and Standard ground; her profile — track the pace, quicken when asked — fits this race shape perfectly and the Balding yard is firing at 7/57 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Two wins from five recent starts, including a narrow but decisive handicap success at Wetherby last time off a 1lb lower mark — Nanoscience showed a willing attitude and acts over today's distance on a sound surface. Our top-rated runner here by a clear margin, she is progressive and more can be expected.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator in the lowest-rated horse in the field at OR 65; placed three times at seven furlongs on Soft but yet to win at the trip, and the natural closing style is complicated here by the likelihood she will not get the honest gallop needed to close from the rear in a race that Shushu can control from the front.
runners_data.comment: Off 38 days and yet to win in her last five starts, Who Wants Me showed adequate form when held off the pace at Hamilton despite a slow start; suits 7f on soft and good. First-time tongue-tie adds a variable, but our figures rank her joint-last here — an unlikely threat without a jump in form.

races.paceDynamic: Shushu is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she is expected to bowl along in front at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on Good to Firm ground at Carlisle over seven furlongs. Nanoscience will likely track her in a prominent position, giving the race a clear leader–stalker dynamic rather than a contested early gallop. The hold-up contingent — Rogue Attraction, Mostar Dreams, Donna Nook and Who Wants Me — will be racing from the rear, though Donna Nook and Who Wants Me are natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map only because the field holds more closers than the visual layout can place at the back; neither is likely to secure a forward position in practice. A sustainable, uncontested pace set by Shushu most directly favours the prominent-to-leader profile, with Nanoscience ideally placed to exploit any fade from the front, while true closers will need the fractions to be fast enough to close — a condition that a lone, uncontested front-runner is unlikely to create.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shushu Controls, Nanoscience Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Shushu leads unchallenged and Nanoscience tracks her throughout before challenging in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Shushu leads unchallenged and Nanoscience tracks her throughout before challenging in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Shushu Wires The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Shushu sets a truly controlled pace and sustains her effort to the line, with no closer able to reel her in.
scenarios.body: If Shushu sets a truly controlled pace and sustains her effort to the line, with no closer able to reel her in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp A Fading Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Shushu sets a stronger-than-expected pace and ties up inside the final furlong, allowing the hold-up runners to close.
scenarios.body: If Shushu sets a stronger-than-expected pace and ties up inside the final furlong, allowing the hold-up runners to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Exploit Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If Donna Nook or Who Wants Me manage to secure a closer mid-division position and produce a strong late run that bridges the gap.
scenarios.body: If Donna Nook or Who Wants Me manage to secure a closer mid-division position and produce a strong late run that bridges the gap.

watchPoints.text: Nanoscience: watch whether P J McDonald takes her straight to Shushu's shoulder from the gate — if she slots in second early, she is ideally placed for a prominent-racer win in a pace-controlled race.

Shushu: monitor whether Ray Dawson elects to dictate or sit just off a rival — if she leads freely and is not pressured through the first half, the fractions will be slow enough to make life very hard for the hold-up horses.

Rogue Attraction: 236 days off the track for a two-year-old filly stepping up to seven furlongs is a major concern; watch the market for any signs of confidence from the Bethell yard before committing to her claims.

Mostar Dreams: top weight and a 138-day absence from an Irish yard (Keatley at 2/9 in 14 days) means her fitness level is genuinely uncertain — watch her in the paddock and the early betting moves for clues.

Donna Nook and Who Wants Me: both are true closers who the pace map has pushed forward for space reasons — if Shushu sets a slow tempo, watch whether either can find the room to accelerate late or whether the race runs away from them before the two-furlong pole.
